segments.title: Chương 42: 0042 [Không Thiếu Tiền]
segments.content:
Boss Shi was pretty hardcore about playing Legend of Mir.

Never mind how much money he spent on gear; he even had his own dedicated team of power-levelers.

At first, he hired only one power-leveler, but later found the leveling speed to be insufficient, so he hired several more to play in shifts.

Since there was a power-leveling team, there had to be a team leader, who served as Boss Shi's "game secretary."

This game secretary was also a former power-leveler. His real name is hard to verify; when interviewed, he always used the pseudonym "Xie Ming." Later on, he became an administrator for the Zhengtu development team.

We'll just call him Xie Ming for now.

"Brother Ming."

"Morning, Brother Ming."

As Boss Shi's game secretary and the leader of the power-leveling team, Xie Ming arrived at the gaming office early in the morning.

He checked the gear and gold coins obtained the previous night, signed off for two power-levelers to switch shifts, and then turned on his computer to hang out in chat rooms.

Life was so damn boring!

Because Legend of Mir hadn't been updated in over half a year, Boss Shi's account had long reached level 46, and hitting level 47 seemed a distant prospect.

Boss Shi himself had grown a bit weary of it, often not showing up for half a month at a time. When he did occasionally play, he would just lead his power-leveling team to PK, logging off once he'd had his fill of killing people. If he was the one killed, he'd burst into a tirade of curses.

Often, both sides in a PK battle would get heated, resorting to fighting again with overpowered hacks, and frequently getting their accounts banned for using them.

Once, Boss Shi even went all the way to Shanda's headquarters to personally ask Boss Chen to unban his account.

After hanging out in chat rooms until noon, Xie Ming had lunch, came back, signed off for the power-levelers to switch shifts, and then lay down on the sofa for a nap.

The two power-levelers on duty teamed up to grind mobs and level up for Boss Shi.

The other power-levelers did whatever they wanted; some even went to play Westward Journey Online II.

While bored to tears, they also feared being fired by Boss Shi.

After all, Boss Shi was playing less and less himself, and there was no telling when he might lose interest in Legend of Mir entirely.

The day idled by quickly until evening.

Xie Ming went to dinner with the off-duty power-levelers. When he came back to sign for the shift change, one of the power-levelers who had just finished said, "Brother Ming, Abyss Legend is launching tonight. A lot of players are planning to go check it out together."

"What's Abyss Legend?" Xie Ming asked.

"You don't know yet?"

"Is it that famous?"

"For the past few days, many players in Legend of Mir have been talking about it. I even went to the forums to check out the threads."

"..."

Intrigued by what his subordinate said, Xie Ming went back to his computer, logged onto 17173, and soon found himself laughing as he read the threads, even joining the discussion to post a few replies.

He resonated with the sentiments in the posts.

His resentment ran deeper than that of an ordinary player. If Shanda never released an update, Xie Ming could lose his job!

"Brother Ming, let's go check it out together," one of the power-levelers said with a grin.

Xie Ming thought for a moment, then gave his orders, "Those who have the midnight shift, go get some sleep now. Those currently on duty, stick to playing Legend of Mir. The rest of you can play a bit of Abyss Legend."

The power-levelers had a lot of freedom. They could even take time off for personal matters occasionally, as long as they arranged for cover among themselves.

With high-spec computers and fast broadband, they quickly downloaded the game, chatting while they waited for Abyss Legend to launch.

Just as they got into the game, Boss Shi arrived.

And he reeked of alcohol.

"Boss!"

"Boss!"

"..."

The power-levelers all stood up to greet him.

The one operating the main account even gave up his computer, conveniently swiveling the chair halfway around.

Boss Shi plopped down.

The others quickly logged into Legend of Mir, instantly transforming from power-levelers to gaming companions.

Boss Shi was in a bad mood today. The moment he got in-game, he started killing people everywhere, and the power-levelers could only follow him, hacking away indiscriminately.

Boss Shi had already decided to sell Nao Bai Jin and Golden Partner, with the final round of negotiations having just concluded a few days ago.

Today, unhappy with Boss Shi's bullheaded decision, his start-up partner had gotten into a huge fight with him!

A dinner meeting ended on a sour note.

"Where's my wine?"

In the middle of his killing spree, Boss Shi threw his mouse aside and yelled.

Xie Ming hurried off to get some red wine and a glass.

Boss Shi would later develop a taste for sauce-aroma baijiu, but at this stage, he preferred red wine. A glass of expensive red wine was poured, and without even letting it breathe, he gulped it down.

The power-levelers were so scared they didn't dare breathe loudly, all of them seeing that the boss was in a terrible mood tonight.

A max-level player who had been cut down by Boss Shi lay on the ground, not leaving, and cursed, "F*ck your mom, let's duel one-on-one if you have the guts!"

"Piss off!"

Boss Shi typed in reply.

The other player continued to lie there as a corpse, cursing relentlessly. Boss Shi stood over the body, trading insults with him.

The power-levelers also ran over, surrounding the corpse and helping their boss curse out the enemy.

The other player couldn't take the verbal assault and said angrily, "I'm done with this sh*tty game. I'm deleting my character right now and going to play Abyss Legend. Why don't you f*cking chase me there and kill me again!"

With that, the corpse disappeared.

Having lost his target to vent on, Boss Shi leaned back in his computer chair and closed his eyes to rest.

The power-levelers didn't dare to speak, all sitting silently in front of their respective computers.

After a while, Xie Ming noticed that the boss had fallen asleep. He went to get a blanket and covered Boss Shi to prevent him from catching a cold.

"Brother Ming, what should we do?"

"You guys go do your own thing, just don't make any noise. I'll watch him here. Those who don't have a shift, go home and sleep."

An unknown amount of time passed before Boss Shi was woken by the urge to pee.

He went to the restroom and came back, but instead of playing the game, he asked Xie Ming, "What do you think about me making a game?"

Xie Ming replied, "Boss, I don't know anything about business, only how to play games."

Boss Shi said with a smile, "One of these days, I'll set up a game development team, and you'll be in charge of managing them."

Xie Ming said uneasily, "But I don't know anything about management either."

Boss Shi said, "You've managed the power-leveling team quite well."

Xie Ming didn't know how to respond. He felt a sense of anticipation, but also trepidation.

This was no whim on Boss Shi's part; he had had a plan for a while. After poaching a game development team, Boss Shi himself would act as the game planner, coming up with all those pay-to-win schemes in Zhengtu.

In about twenty more days, once he had sorted out the internal profit-sharing of his company, Boss Shi would sign the papers to sell Nao Bai Jin and Golden Partner, then scout everywhere for a development team to go all-in on making games.

Boss Shi finally noticed something was off. Looking at the chat box, he saw people were still talking about some Abyss Legend.

"LMAO, even a private server can have its server crash from traffic."

"I just got back from 17173, the forums over there are buzzing."

"I'm so awesome, watch the formation."

"I'm so awesome, watch the formation."

"What the f*ck are you spamming for? This is Legend of Mir. If you want to spam, go play your private server."

"..."

Xie Ming said, "A lot of players have gone to play the private server. Those who can't get in are on the forums spamming posts. There are also people who aren't playing the private server, but just went to the forums for the drama."

Under Xie Ming's guidance, Boss Shi logged onto the forums.

As he browsed the threads, he listened to Xie Ming explain the whole story.

After a long while, Boss Shi stared at a few popular threads and said, "There are traces of manipulation here. You wouldn't notice without careful study. The people behind this private server are definitely experts."

Xie Ming was surprised, "You mean these threads were intentionally manipulated?"

Boss Shi browsed a bit more. "I'm not sure either. It could just be a coincidence. But it's too much of a coincidence. I don't believe in such coincidences. Have you guys downloaded this private server?"

"We have," said Xie Ming.

Boss Shi immediately ordered, "Those who haven't gone home, all of you get in there with me."

Half an hour later, Boss Shi, who never played private servers, was actually having a blast in Abyss Legend.

It couldn't be helped. He had long grown tired of the official Legend of Mir, which hadn't been updated in half a year. The changes in the private server, on the other hand, felt fresh and new to him.

Boss Shi and his power-levelers finished the quest to obtain entry tickets together and then excitedly ran off to clear the Abyss dungeon.

The entry tickets obtained from the quest had a line of small text at the bottom: Quest Item, Untradeable.

At the Veteran NPC, many players were shouting, "Team for Woma Abyss, solo players only, solo players only! Gear-snatching teams, piss off~~~"

Boss Shi stood there watching for a moment, then said to Xie Ming, "Tell them to come back to run the Abyss. I'll reimburse their taxi fares!"

The maximum number of people in a party was 10, but if you teamed up with strangers, disputes over gear were bound to happen after killing the boss.

Xie Ming made several calls in quick succession. The power-levelers who had just gotten home hurriedly hailed taxis to come back and accompany their boss.

After playing for nearly another two hours, they had leveled up everyone and improved their gear. One boss, one team leader, and six power-levelers, a total of eight people, entered the dungeon.

They were teleported directly to a corner of the Woma Sect Leader's hall.

There seemed to be an invisible barrier here. The other areas were densely packed with monsters, but this corner was very safe.

"Damn, this place is full of Abyss Mutated Monsters!"

"Take it slow. Mages, cast Fire Wall. Taoists, use Poison. Warriors and Skeleton babies, go tank."

"The skeletons aren't high enough level, and the Taoists only have level 0 Heal."

"I'm almost out of red pots and Sun Water!"

"I'm dead, I'm dead. Our levels are too low and our gear isn't good enough. We probably need a full set of Abyss Overpowered gear to do this!"

"..."

Having killed only half of the monsters on the screen, Boss Shi's eight-man team was completely wiped out.

Some could have left by using a Town Portal Scroll, but since the boss had already died, they could only stay behind to perish with him.

Xie Ming opened his inventory and burst out laughing, "A mob dropped an entry ticket and I picked it up. This run wasn't a loss for me, I've already made back the ticket cost... uh," he abruptly stopped laughing, "Boss, are we going again?"

Boss Shi was already adding a QQ contact to top up, "Recharge for entry tickets, let's go again! The monsters in here have a higher chance of dropping mutated gear. A few more runs and we can get a full set of low-level mutated gear. Remember to pick up the gear with the red glow, and portal back to town if you can't hold on. Once we've upgraded our gear, we'll definitely be able to kill the Abyss Woma Sect Leader!"

This playstyle was truly one of someone who wasn't short on cash.

When he first started playing Legend of Mir, he lost a PK battle and was so pissed off that he immediately forked out 50,000 RMB to buy gear.

"Recharging 3,000 RMB. My surname is Shi. Tell your boss to come here," Boss Shi typed quickly.

A whale has arrived, recharging 3,000 RMB. Tell Old Wang to come out and give us more chapters
